A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work, renamed from EVTAR to RefTon, and all supplied pages are readable. However, v4 ends after the references despite citing Appendices A–C; their promised data details, DressCode subset results and additional qualitative examples cannot be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original VITON-HD and DressCode experiments, including mask/reference variants and mixed-VFR training results in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark results and adds StreetTryOn evaluations and position-index ablations in Tables 2 and 4.

M1.justification: Both versions use Flux-Kontext with LoRA, two-stage synthetic training, 50% masked/unmasked input sampling, 25% reference inclusion, and resolution-scaled three-channel position indices. v4 names and explains this existing design more explicitly; its additional evaluations do not establish a changed model or training objective.

E1.justification: v4 adds StreetTryOn evaluation across shop-to-street, person-to-person, person-to-street and street-to-street scenarios. Its P2P tests omit the standalone garment image, substantially extending evaluated input conditions. VITON-HD, DressCode and the mixed-VFR source datasets remain.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 adds mask-free CatVTON, Any2AnyTryon and TryOffDiff comparisons. Table 2 compares against StreetTryOn and OmniVTON, while the DressCode qualitative comparison adds CAT-DM and OOTDiffusion to the comparators displayed in v1 Figure 7. These materially broaden comparison coverage.

E3.justification: The stated existing splits, training budgets, metrics and evaluation resizing remain unchanged. Added procedures include garment-image-free P2P testing and original-versus-rescaled position indexing at 0.5 and 0.25 condition scales. The StreetTryOn comparison in v4 Table 2 still specifies mask inputs.

E4.justification: v4 adds a controlled position-index ablation across two condition resolutions and masked/unmasked settings (Table 4), plus qualitative analysis of mask errors involving handbags and retained leg regions (Figure 7). The four mask/reference configurations discussed in its new ablation section already had numerical results in v1.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v4's additional experiments continue the existing single-value metric reporting practice.

E6.justification: The matched aggregate benchmark and mixed-VFR scores are unchanged. v4 adds mask-free comparator results, StreetTryOn scores, position-index ablation results and qualitative examples; for example, Table 2 reports street-to-street FID of 16.452 for RefTon versus 23.470 for OmniVTON. Retention of v1's DressCode subset results cannot be verified because v4's referenced Appendix B is absent.

T1.justification: The continuity equation, conditional flow-matching objective and sampling ODE in Equations 1–3 remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies substantive theorems or proofs; the unrelated theoretical claims removed from v1's conclusion were not developed into formal results.

C1.justification: v4 replaces v1's unrelated conclusion claiming time/class-conditioning removal and geometric diffusion insights with a conclusion about reference-guided virtual try-on. Its contribution list also explicitly foregrounds Flux-Kontext adaptation, rescaled indexing and reference-data generation, while retaining the central reference-assisted and mask-free try-on claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of shortcut copying, mask-induced failures and reference-only garment extraction in the new P2P tests. It also qualifies v1's misleading statement that the mixed model was not trained on VITON-HD or DressCode: v4 correctly says it was not trained on them individually.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies CLIP-feature duplicate filtering and Qwen2.5-VL rejection of distorted, unclear or back-facing images, expanding v1's general filtering description. It changes the repository pointer and explicitly advertises dataset availability, without establishing that experimental settings changed. Further details promised in Appendix A are unavailable.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning against mask-free and person-to-person approaches, including OmniTry, Any2AnyTryon, TryOffDiff and ViTON-GUN. It explicitly attributes the two-stage strategy to CatVTON and distinguishes its independent condition indexing from Any2AnyTryon's concatenated-canvas approach, sharpening the relationship to close prior work.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming EVTAR to RefTon, v4 extensively rewrites the abstract, related work and method explanations, reorganizes training details between Sections 3.2–3.3, introduces a dedicated ablation section and replaces the conclusion. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column layout, merges v1 Tables 1–2, restructures the mixed-training table, redraws the indexing and reference-generation diagrams, and expands qualitative comparison panels. It also adds StreetTryOn and ablation tables and simplifies the opening reference-effect figure, removing its separate training-only-reference column.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens support through more relevant mask-free comparisons and component tests, improves prior-work attribution, and repairs v1's unrelated conclusion. However, missing Appendices A–C limit completeness, and some new interpretations overreach: Table 4 contradicts the claimed universal indexing improvement, with mask-free FID worsening from 5.35 to 5.37 at 0.25 scale. The available evidence supports a modest net improvement.
